_comment: Registry for scripts/check_retired_claims.py. See kn-mxxu for why it exists.
RETIRED = false, must never reappear in any wording. Patterns are deliberately
SEMANTIC (negation near a capability noun), not the literal sentence that was
removed. The 2026-08-22 fix failed precisely because it matched one phrasing.
ALLOWED = currently true, and `evidence` names the code that keeps it true. If
that code changes, the guard reports the claim as unsupported rather than
letting a once-accurate sentence rot quietly.
Narrow ON PURPOSE, calibrated against real content rather than guessed.
The family this guard polices is: what THE CONTROL PLANE does or does not
do with YOUR cluster's credentials and API. A broader tripwire flagged 13
sentences, nearly all of them about the operator, the app, or other
products -- and an allowlist full of unrelated prose is how a guard becomes
noise that people learn to wave through.
'kubenest' and 'we' are deliberately NOT subjects: they match company-voice
sentences all over the site. If the claim is about the control plane, it
says so.
tripwire.subject: \b(the\s+)?(backend|control\s+plane)\b

retired.because: The control plane stores a cluster-scoped bearer the agent advertises, plus the API server address and its CA (kubenest-backend app/models/cluster.py, kubenest_sa_token).
A compromised control plane holds a decryptable bearer, the API server address and its CA on one row, and can build a client in one line. Removing call sites removed routine use, not capability.
patterns: compromised[^.]{0,60}\b(cannot|can't|could not|couldn't|is unable to|no ability to)\b[^.]{0,60}(kubectl|kubernetes api|api call|api calls|arbitrary)

retired.because: It is not. One credential per cluster is persisted in PostgreSQL, along with the API server address and CA.

Three of four direct paths are closed; ArgoCD cluster registration still reaches the tenant API directly. An unqualified 'all operations' or 'every operation' claim is false until the fourth path closes.

allowed.says: For application, addon and component-secret operations the control plane builds no Kubernetes client for your cluster at all.
allowed.true_because: kn-2fz2, kn-37n5 and kn-qh3g closed three of kn-cjqw's four direct paths. This is the ONE claim in this family that is currently true, and it is true only while the client builders stay deleted -- which is exactly why it carries evidence rather than a note.

Narrowly true and kept deliberately: no kubeconfig is uploaded. It is QUALIFIED in place -- the stored bearer is named in the same block -- because standing alone a reader takes it to mean no credential is held, which is false. If the qualification is ever deleted, this sentence becomes the Q2 failure again.

_comment: Patterns that mark a sentence as NOT a claim about our trust boundary.
These are applied ONLY to the unclassified tripwire, never to the retired
patterns -- so an exclusion can reduce noise but can NEVER hide a claim
already known to be false. That asymmetry is the whole safety property.
Each entry earned its place by producing a false positive on real content.

subject is the in-cluster agent; 'backend' appears only as an object
